unit.title: Prepare customer accounts and deal with departures

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is a guest folio?
options: The card a guest fills in and signs when they arrive
The list of all guests leaving today
A record of a guest's charges and payments
The folder that holds the guest's key card

questions.stem: A guest signs a bar bill to their room. When should the charge be posted to their folio?
options: As soon as possible, before they check out
Only at the end of the month, when accounts close
When the guest asks to see their bill
After the guest has gone home

questions.stem: Why is the signed bar or restaurant bill (the voucher) kept after the charge is posted?
options: So it can be given to the next guest
So the waiter can work out the tips
So the kitchen can plan the next menu
As proof if the guest asks about the charge

questions.stem: What is the main job of the night audit?
options: To check the day's charges and payments are right
To clean the lobby and the pool area while guests are sleeping
To count the guests' luggage in the store
To make the breakfast orders for the morning

questions.stem: A guest paid a deposit when they booked. What happens to it at check-out?
options: It is kept by the property as a booking fee
It is added on top of the final bill
It is taken off the amount the guest owes
It is paid back in cash before they pay

questions.stem: At check-in, a hold is put on a guest's card to cover charges during the stay. What is this hold called?
options: A cash refund
A paid-out
A pre-authorisation
A city ledger transfer

questions.stem: A guest's charges have gone over the credit limit the property allows. What usually happens?
options: The guest's room is cleaned last each day
The charges are hidden until check-out
The guest is politely asked for a payment
The guest is asked to leave at once

questions.stem: A company has agreed to pay for its staff member's room later, by invoice. Where is the bill sent at check-out?
options: To the guest's home address
To the cashier's own drawer
To the bank as a loan
To the city ledger

questions.stem: Before a guest's bill is charged to their company, what must the front office have?
options: A phone call from the guest's friend
The guest's word that the company will pay
Written approval from the company
A copy of the guest's airline ticket

questions.stem: A company pays for a guest's room only, and the guest pays for meals and drinks. How is this usually set up?
options: All charges go on one folio, paid by the company
The guest pays for everything and claims it back
The meals are added to the room rate each night
Two folios, one for each payer

questions.stem: At an all-inclusive property, what does a guest usually still pay for at check-out?
options: Extras outside the package, like the spa
Every meal and drink taken during the stay
The cost of cleaning the room each day
The pool towels and sun loungers used

questions.stem: Which report tells the front desk which guests are due to leave today?
options: The arrivals list
The departures list
The housekeeping rota
The night audit summary

questions.stem: Why are the folios of guests leaving tomorrow checked the night before?
options: So housekeeping can start cleaning those rooms early
So mistakes are fixed before the guest is at the desk
So the guests can be asked to leave earlier
So the rooms can be sold again at a higher price

questions.stem: A guest asks to keep the room three hours after the normal check-out time. What should you do?
options: Say yes straight away without checking anything
Check room availability and the policy, then reply
Tell the guest it is never allowed
Charge them for a full extra night without telling them

questions.stem: What is a "late charge"?
options: A fee for arriving after midnight
A charge for a late check-out room
A charge that comes after check-out
Money a guest owes from a past stay

questions.stem: How can the front desk help to prevent late charges at check-out?
options: By closing the bar early on departure day
By asking about any charges made this morning
By not letting departing guests have breakfast at all
By charging every guest a fixed extra amount

questions.stem: A guest comes to the desk to check out. How should you confirm which room they are in?
options: Ask for their name and key card quietly
Call out the room number to the lobby
Guess from the luggage they are carrying
Ask the bell attendant to tell you

questions.stem: Why do you give the guest the folio to check before they pay?
options: So they can add a tip for the manager
So they can sign it for the night auditor
So they can choose which charges to pay
So they agree the charges are correct

questions.stem: A guest says a dinner charge on the folio is not theirs. What should you do first?
options: Check the signed bill (voucher) with them
Tell them they must pay all the charges
Take the charge off at once with no checks
Ask the restaurant to call the guest later

questions.stem: A charge was posted by mistake and must be taken off a folio. Who usually approves this correction (an allowance)?
options: The front office supervisor
The guest who is checking out
The bell attendant on duty
Any front desk agent who is free

questions.stem: A guest's folio total is J$48,600 and they will pay by card. What should you check on the terminal before handing it to the guest?
options: That the amount keyed is J$48,600
That the guest's PIN is shown on the screen
That the tip has been added already
That the card number has been written down

questions.stem: For this question only, use a practice rate of J$150 = US$1. A folio total is J$30,000 and the guest wants to pay in US$ cash. How much is that?
A guest pays the folio in full. What should the balance on the folio be after payment?
options: The same as the deposit paid
The total of the room nights
The GCT at the current rate
Zero (J$0.00)

questions.stem: What should the guest receive after paying the folio?
options: A blank registration card for the next stay
The key card for their room, to keep
A copy of another guest's bill as a sample
A receipt or a copy of the settled folio

questions.stem: Why do you ask a departing guest to return their key card?
options: So the guest can be charged for a new one
So the bell attendant can carry the luggage
So the guest cannot claim the deposit back
For room security, and so it can be reused

questions.stem: A guest has used a safe deposit box at the front desk. What should you check at check-out?
options: That the guest has paid a tip to the cashier
That the box is left locked with items inside
That the box key is kept by the guest
That the box is emptied and the key returned

questions.stem: After a guest checks out, what should the front desk do with the room status?
options: Leave it shown as occupied until the next morning
Change it to vacant dirty and tell housekeeping
Leave it the same until the guest calls
Mark it as out of order for a week

questions.stem: Why should housekeeping be told quickly when a guest has left?
options: So the room can be cleaned and sold again
So the guest's bill can be made a little larger
So the minibar can be filled for free
So staff can use the room for a rest

questions.stem: A departing guest has heavy bags and a flight to catch. What can the front desk offer?
options: To keep the bags until the guest's next visit
Bell help and a booked transfer
A discount if they carry the bags themselves
A later flight booked without asking them

questions.stem: A guest has checked out but wants to leave bags at the property until the afternoon. What should you do?
options: Leave the bags in the lobby where they are
Tag them and keep them in the luggage room
Put them back in the room the guest has left
Ask another guest to watch the bags

questions.stem: What is express check-out?
options: Letting a guest leave without paying the bill
Moving a guest to a faster lift at check-out
Leaving the property before the check-in time
Paying by card on file, without queueing at the desk

questions.stem: A guest has left the property without paying the bill. What is this guest often called?
options: A walk-in
A no-show
A skipper
A stayover

questions.stem: You think a guest has left without paying. What should you do?
options: Chase the guest's car down the road
Report it to your supervisor at once
Pay the bill yourself so it balances
Post the bill to another guest's folio

questions.stem: A caller says they are a guest's friend and asks you to read out the guest's bill. What should you do?
options: Read out the bill, since they seem to know the guest
Email the bill to the address the caller gives
Politely refuse and offer to take a message
Fax a copy to the caller's office straight away

questions.stem: Why should a guest's folio be printed or shown only to the guest who owns it?
options: Because the printer is slow and paper costs a lot of money
Because it holds private details about the guest
Because other guests might want the same price
Because the night auditor must sign it first

questions.stem: A tour group is leaving together. The tour company pays for the rooms. What should each group member settle at the desk?
options: Their own extra charges, such as drinks
The full room bill for the whole group
A share of the tour guide's wages for the week
Nothing, as the group leader pays tips

questions.stem: How should you end the check-out with a guest?
options: Turn away to serve the next guest at once
Tell them to hurry so the room can be cleaned
Say nothing, as the bill is now paid
Thank them by name and invite them back

questions.stem: During check-out, a guest says the air conditioning was noisy all week. What should you do?
options: Say that every room has the same problem
Tell the guest it is not the front desk's job
Apologise, record it and tell maintenance
Offer a free stay without asking anyone

questions.stem: Why might the front desk update a guest's history record at check-out?
options: To make sure they pay more on their next visit
To note likes and needs for the next stay
To share their details with other businesses
To remove their name from the fire list

questions.stem: A guest booked five nights but wants to leave after three. What should you check?
options: The booking terms for early departure
If the guest's luggage will fit in a taxi
If the restaurant is still serving lunch
If the guest has visited Jamaica before

questions.stem: A guest asks why GCT is shown on the folio. What should you say?
options: It is the tax on sales, at the current rate
It is a charge the property adds for the staff
It is a fee for paying with a foreign card
It is a charge for using the room safe

questions.stem: A guest pays a J$ folio with US$ cash. Which exchange rate do you use?
options: The rate the guest found on the internet
The rate from the guest's home country
The property's rate for that day
Any rate that makes the sum easy

questions.stem: A guest asks the desk to pay a taxi driver J$3,000 for them and add it to their bill. What is this called?
options: A late charge
An allowance
A refund
A paid-out

questions.stem: A guest on today's departures list has not come to the desk by check-out time. What should you do first?
options: Charge them for another full night at once
Send security to open the room and pack the bags
Call the room politely to check their plans
Put their bags in the lobby for them

questions.stem: Why does the front desk write important notes in a log book at the end of each shift?
options: So the next shift can decorate the desk
So the manager can mark staff absent
So guests can read about other guests
So the next shift can follow up

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Many properties keep reservations, rooms and guest accounts on one computer system. What do the letters PMS stand for?
What is the card or form a guest fills in and signs when they check in?
A folio shows J$12,000 of charges and a J$5,000 deposit already paid. How much does the guest still owe, in J$?
What is the account called that holds a group's shared charges, such as the rooms paid by the tour company?
What is the time by which guests must leave their rooms on the day they depart called?
What is a guest called who is staying on and is not leaving today?
What is it called when a guest asks to keep the room after the normal check-out time?
What is it called when a guest leaves before the last night they booked?
What is the small fridge of drinks and snacks in a guest room, which often causes late charges, called?
Which kind of payment card lets the guest pay now and pay the bank back later?
What is the three-letter code for the United States dollar?
What do you ask to see to confirm a guest's identity, such as a passport or driver's licence?
What is the job title of the staff member who carries guests' luggage at a hotel?
What is the name of the international airport in Montego Bay that many departing visitors use?
What short card or form can a guest fill in to give feedback about their stay?

essays.stem: Explain how charges get onto a guest's folio during the stay, and why they must be posted quickly and correctly.
essays.modelAnswer: When a guest signs a bill in the restaurant, bar, spa or laundry, the outlet sends the signed voucher, or the charge goes through the POS straight to the property management system. The front desk or the system posts each charge to the right folio, checking the guest's name and room number and the amount. Room and tax are posted each night at the night audit, and the auditor checks that all the day's charges and payments are right. Paid-outs, such as a taxi paid for the guest, are posted with a signed slip. Charges must be posted quickly so that they are on the folio before the guest checks out, or they become late charges that may never be paid. They must be correct because a wrong charge upsets the guest, wastes time at check-out and loses the property money.
markingPoints: Outlets send signed vouchers or the POS posts the charge
Checks name, room and amount before posting
Room and tax posted nightly and checked at the night audit
Posted quickly to avoid late charges and lost money
Posted correctly to avoid disputes and keep guests happy

essays.stem: Describe how the front desk prepares for the day's departures.
essays.modelAnswer: The front desk prints the departures list, which shows the guests due to leave, their rooms, how they will pay and any notes. The night before, or early in the morning, each departing folio is checked: all charges are posted, the room rate is right, deposits are credited and any company billing has written approval. Mistakes are corrected with supervisor approval. Folios may be printed and ready, or sent for express check-out. The desk checks for requests such as late check-out, luggage help, wake-up calls and airport transfers, and books them. The bell attendants are told the times for luggage pick-up, and housekeeping is given the list so they can plan the cleaning. The cashier makes sure there is enough float, including US$ if needed, and that the card terminal works.
markingPoints: Prints and reads the departures list
Checks each departing folio: charges, rate, deposits, billing approval
Corrects errors with approval and prepares folios or express check-out
Arranges late check-outs, luggage, wake-up calls and transfers
Tells bell and housekeeping; checks float and terminal

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, a full check-out for a guest who is paying by card.
essays.modelAnswer: I greet the guest with a smile and use their name. I confirm their identity by asking for their name and key card, without saying the room number aloud. I ask if they have used the minibar or signed any bills this morning, and post any last charges. I print the folio and go through it with the guest so they can see each charge, the deposit and the GCT. If they agree, I key the total into the card terminal and check the amount with them. The guest inserts or taps the card and enters their own PIN. When the payment is approved, I give them the receipt and the settled folio showing a zero balance. I collect the key cards, check the safe deposit box is emptied, offer help with luggage and transport, thank them and invite them back. Then I update the room status and tell housekeeping.
markingPoints: Greets the guest and confirms identity without saying the room number aloud
Asks about and posts any last charges
Goes through the folio with the guest
Takes the card payment correctly and gives a receipt and zero-balance folio
Collects keys, offers help, says farewell, updates room status and tells housekeeping

essays.stem: A guest disputes a charge on the folio at check-out. Explain how you deal with it.
essays.modelAnswer: I stay calm and polite and listen to the guest without arguing. I apologise for the trouble and tell them I will check it straight away. I find the signed voucher or the POS record for that charge and look at it with the guest, checking the date, the time, the signature and the room number. If the charge is correct, I explain it kindly and show the guest the proof. If it was posted by mistake, or the guest is still unhappy, I call my supervisor, who decides whether to make an allowance to take it off. The allowance is recorded with the reason and approved with the supervisor's signature or code. I print a new folio for the guest to check and thank them for their patience. I never remove a charge without approval, and I report the mistake so it does not happen again.
markingPoints: Stays calm, listens and apologises
Finds the signed voucher or record and checks it with the guest
Explains a correct charge kindly with the proof
Gets a supervisor to approve and record any allowance
Prints a new folio, thanks the guest and reports the mistake

essays.stem: Describe the different ways a guest may settle their account at check-out, with one check you make for each.
essays.modelAnswer: A guest may pay by cash in J$. I count the money, check the notes are genuine and count the change back. A guest may pay by cash in US$. I use only the property's rate for the day, show the working and record both currencies. A guest may pay by credit or debit card. I check that the amount on the terminal is right and that the guest enters their own PIN, and I wait for approval. The bill may go to the guest's company through the city ledger. I check that there is written approval from the company and that the guest signs the folio. Some guests pay with a voucher from a tour company. I check that it is valid and for this property and stay. For any method, I give a receipt and make sure the folio shows a zero balance.
markingPoints: J$ cash: checks notes and counts the change back
US$ cash: uses the property's rate and records both currencies
Card: checks the amount, guest keys own PIN, waits for approval
Company billing or voucher: written approval or a valid voucher, folio signed
Gives a receipt and checks the balance is zero

essays.stem: A guest wants to pay part of the folio in US$ cash and the rest by card. Explain how you deal with this.
essays.modelAnswer: I first tell the guest the total in J$ and agree how much they want to pay in US$. I use only the property's exchange rate for the day and tell the guest the rate. I count the US$ notes in front of the guest, check they are genuine and in good condition, and work out what they are worth in J$, showing the working. I post the US$ payment to the folio, so the balance goes down. I then tell the guest the balance still owed in J$ and key that exact amount into the card terminal. The guest inserts or taps the card and enters their PIN. When it is approved, I print the folio showing both payments and a zero balance, and give the guest the receipts. At the cash-up the US$ is counted and recorded separately.
markingPoints: Agrees the amounts with the guest
Uses the property's rate for the day and shows the working
Counts and checks the US$ notes
Posts the cash payment, then charges the exact balance to the card
Folio shows both payments and a zero balance; US$ recorded separately

essays.stem: Explain how you protect guest privacy and the property's security during check-out.
essays.modelAnswer: I never say a guest's room number aloud, because others in the lobby could hear it and go to the room. I confirm who the guest is by asking for their name and key card, or ID if needed. I show and print the folio only for the guest who owns it, and I do not leave folios on the desk where others can read them. I never read out charges or give out a guest's details over the phone. I never ask for a card PIN or write down card numbers. I collect all key cards so that nobody can get into the room after the guest has left, and I make sure the safe deposit box is emptied and its key returned. Guest records are kept on the system with a password, and printed papers with guest details are shredded as the property says.
markingPoints: Does not say room numbers aloud; checks identity
Shows and prints the folio only for its owner and keeps papers out of view
Does not give out guest details or card details
Collects all keys and checks the safe deposit box is emptied
Keeps records secure and disposes of papers safely

essays.stem: Explain what the front desk must do after a guest has checked out and left.
essays.modelAnswer: First I change the room status on the system to vacant dirty and tell housekeeping, so the room can be cleaned, inspected and sold again. I check that the folio is settled with a zero balance, and that any company bill has gone to the city ledger with its signed papers. I file the vouchers and receipts with the folio. If a late charge arrives, such as a minibar or breakfast bill, I tell my supervisor, who decides whether to charge the guest's card, if the guest allowed it, or to write it off. I update the guest history with notes such as likes, complaints or special requests. Any complaint the guest made is passed on to the right department. I check the luggage store and the lost property for anything the guest left behind.
markingPoints: Changes the room status and tells housekeeping
Checks the folio is settled and company bills are sent with papers
Files vouchers and receipts
Deals with late charges through the supervisor
Updates guest history, passes on complaints and checks for left property

essays.stem: A guest asks to check out late and to store luggage until an afternoon flight. Explain how you deal with this.
essays.modelAnswer: I thank the guest for asking and check the system to see if the room is needed for an arriving guest. I check the property's policy on late check-out, because there may be a charge for extra hours. If it is possible, I tell the guest the new time and any charge, and note it on the system so housekeeping knows not to clean the room yet. If it is not possible, I apologise and offer to store their luggage and let them use the pool, the lounge or a shower room until they leave. To store the luggage, I count the bags with the guest, tag each one, give the guest the stub and record it in the luggage book, then the bell attendant puts the bags in the locked luggage room. I offer to book a taxi or airport transfer for the right time.
markingPoints: Checks availability and the late check-out policy and any charge
Tells the guest and updates the system and housekeeping
Offers luggage storage and the use of facilities if late check-out is not possible
Counts, tags and records the bags, gives a stub and locks them away
Offers to book transport at the right time

essays.stem: Explain why check-out is important for the guest's last impression of the property, and how you make it a good one.
essays.modelAnswer: Check-out is the last time the guest deals with the property, so it is often what they remember most. A slow or wrong bill can spoil a good holiday, while a warm, quick check-out makes them want to come back and tell friends about Jamaica. To make it a good one, I prepare the folios before the guest comes, so there are few mistakes and little waiting. I greet the guest with a smile, use their name and ask about their stay. I explain the bill clearly and deal with any problem calmly. I offer help with luggage and transport, so they leave on time and without stress. If they had a complaint, I apologise and pass it on. I thank them, wish them a safe journey and invite them back. This is the Team Jamaica spirit of good service to visitors.
markingPoints: It is the last impression and affects return visits and reviews
Prepares folios before so check-out is quick and correct
Greets warmly, uses the name and asks about the stay
Explains the bill clearly and deals with problems calmly
Offers help with luggage and transport, thanks the guest and invites them back

practical1.title: Prepare and check guest folios for tomorrow's departures
practical1.brief: The assessor gives each member two or three made-up guest folios (on the Centre's training property system, a spreadsheet or paper folio sheets) and a pile of signed vouchers from the restaurant, bar, spa and laundry, with deposits, a company billing letter and a tour voucher. Some vouchers have planted mistakes: a wrong room number, a charge posted twice, a missing signature. Each member posts the vouchers to the right folios, finds and lists the mistakes, fills in an allowance form for each correction for the "supervisor" (another member) to approve, credits the deposits, and prints or writes out a final folio for each guest showing the balance owed. The group then makes one departures list for the next day, showing each guest, room, payment method and any requests. Use only made-up guest names and details. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and every member's folios, error list and allowance forms to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Made-up guest folios on a training system, spreadsheet or paper folio sheets
Signed vouchers from the restaurant, bar, spa and laundry, some with planted mistakes
Deposit records, a company billing letter and a tour voucher
Allowance (correction) forms and a departures list form
A calculator, pens and a printer if a computer is used
The day's exchange rate and GCT "at the current rate", as the assessor gives them
photos: The vouchers sorted by guest and room number
Charges posted to a folio, on screen or on paper
The list of mistakes found, with each voucher beside it
A completed and signed allowance form
A deposit credited on a folio
Each member's final folios showing the balance owed
The finished departures list for the next day
checklist: Posted every voucher to the correct folio with the right amount
Found the planted mistakes (wrong room, double posting, missing signature)
Filled in an allowance form for each correction and had it approved
Credited deposits correctly and treated the company billing as the letter allows
Worked out the balance owed correctly for each folio
Completed the departures list with guest, room, payment method and requests
Kept guest details private and worked neatly and accurately
safety: Use only made-up guest names, card numbers and details
Sit at the computer with a straight back and the screen at eye level, and take short breaks
Keep cables tidy and the work area clear
Shred or return all paper folios to the assessor at the end

practical2.title: Role play: check out guests and deal with departure problems
practical2.brief: Set up a mock front desk with a computer or folio sheets, a training or mock card terminal, a cash drawer of training money (J$ and US$ marked "TRAINING"), key cards, a room status board and a luggage store area. Each member, in turn, checks out one "guest" (another member or the assessor) using a scenario card: greet the guest, confirm their identity without saying the room number aloud, ask about last charges, go through the folio, take payment, give a receipt and a zero-balance folio, collect the key cards and say goodbye. Each scenario has one problem to deal with: a disputed charge, part payment in US$ at the rate the assessor gives, a company bill, a late check-out request, or bags to store until a flight. After each check-out, the member updates the room status board and fills in a housekeeping note. Members who are not at the desk play guests, the supervisor or the bell attendant. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the completed forms to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A mock front desk with a computer or folio sheets and a printer
A training or mock card terminal and made-up payment cards
A drawer of training money (J$ and US$ marked "TRAINING")
Key cards, a room status board, housekeeping notes and luggage tags with stubs
Scenario cards with made-up guests and one problem each
The day's exchange rate and late check-out policy, as the assessor gives them
photos: The front desk set up and ready
A member going through the folio with the "guest"
A payment being taken (card, J$ or US$ cash)
The problem being dealt with (for example, a voucher checked for a disputed charge)
The receipt and zero-balance folio handed over, and key cards collected
Bags tagged and stored with the stub given to the guest
The room status board updated and the housekeeping note filled in
checklist: Greeted the guest warmly and used their name
Confirmed identity without saying the room number aloud
Asked about and posted last charges
Went through the folio clearly and took the payment correctly
Dealt with the problem calmly and correctly, calling the supervisor where needed
Gave a receipt and a zero-balance folio and collected the key cards
Updated the room status and told housekeeping
Thanked the guest, offered help with luggage or transport and invited them back
safety: Use only training money and made-up cards and guest details
Lift bags with bent knees and a straight back; get help with heavy ones
Keep the area in front of the desk and the luggage store clear of trip hazards
Keep the cash drawer closed between payments
